    cnt=Counter(seq[i:i+k] for i in range(n-k+1))
    N=sum(cnt.values())
    p={}
    for b in "ACGT": p[b]=seq.count(b)/n
    obs=[];exp=[]

# Report on `region.fasta` (record `>locus_001`)

## What the file contains
A single-sequence FASTA file: **3,000 bp of unambiguous DNA** (only A, C, G, T; no Ns, lowercase, or masked bases), wrapped at 70 characters per line. No annotation, no second record, no hidden text.

## Summary finding
**Nothing in this sequence stands out as a functional or structural feature.** Every signal I tested is what would be expected by chance for a random / non-coding stretch of DNA of this composition. It most closely resembles a computer-generated random sequence (or a non-conserved, featureless intergenic/spacer region).

## Base composition
| Base | Count | % |
|---|---|---|
| A | 883 | 29.4 |
| T | 855 | 28.5 |
| G | 639 | 21.3 |
| C | 623 | 20.8 |

GC content = **42.1 %** (AT-rich). Chargaff parity holds closely (A≈T, G≈C), and local GC content across 100-bp windows only ranges ~31 %–53 % (sd ≈ 4.9 %), i.e. ordinary sampling fluctuation, with no GC-rich or GC-poor "island" (no CpG island either; overall CpG observed/expected = 1.03, and all 16 dinucleotide O/E ratios lie between 0.89 and 1.07).

## Protein-coding potential: essentially none
Scanning all six reading frames (standard genetic code):

- Longest **ATG→stop ORF**: **83 codons (251 bp including the stop), reverse strand, forward coordinates 2103–2353.** Translation: `MIILIPCSVSAHLQISITARFYIFNTQDLKPPLERLNPKLNLIDMLTLFRTLCKGHVPNEKEQEGSLRLELPRSFLEYPVALE*` — no recognizable domain, putative signal, or homology-worthy composition.
- Longest stop-free stretch (any frame): 267 nt (89 codons), forward strand.
- **No forward-strand ORF reaches even 50 codons** (best is 144 nt).

Both figures match the null expectation for random DNA: simulated sequences with the same base composition give a mean longest ORF of ~243 ± 59 nt (observed 249 nt, P ≈ 0.24–0.9 depending on strand). There is therefore **no gene-like signal** here.

## Repeats and secondary structure: none
- **All 15-mers are unique** (2,986 sliding windows, 0 duplicates) — and likewise no repeated 20/25/30/40-mers.
- **No exact direct repeats ≥ 15 bp** in either orientation, and **no near-duplications** (no two ≥ 30 bp windows sharing ≥ 75 % identity, seeded at 12 bp) — so no tandem arrays, no duplicated segments, no low-complexity region.
- **No palindromes or inverted repeats ≥ 12 bp** (0 found), hence **no hairpin/terminator structures**, **no G-quadruplex motifs**, and no i-motif motifs.
- Longest homopolymer run is only **6 bp** (C at 978–983; G at 2384–2389); longest A-run 5 bp (1335–1339), longest T-run 5 bp (907–911).

- Scattered restriction sites only: `GAATTC` (EcoRI) at 1252; `AAGCTT` (HindIII) at 191 and 2407; `TCTAGA` (XbaI) at 2427; etc. — no cluster or meaningful arrangement.

## One weak, non-conclusive observation
Oligomer usage is *slightly more even* than a random shuffle, in the same direction at every k: χ² vs. the mononucleotide-composition expectation was 40 (k=3), 199 (k=4), 921 (k=5), 3886 (k=6), versus shuffled-control means of 54 ± 12, 242 ± 29, 1006 ± 60, and 4073 ± 121; the numbers of 5-mers/6-mers absent from the sequence are also slightly lower than expected (77 vs. 83 ± 8; 2014 vs. 2047 ± 23). This deviation is only ~1.5–2.5 SD and could easily be sampling noise, but it is mild, consistent evidence that the sequence was produced by an even-composition generator rather than drawn from a real genome.

## Bottom line
The region has **no genes, no repeats (direct, inverted, or tandem), no secondary-structure motifs, no CpG island, and no regulatory motifs beyond chance expectation**; its composition, k-mer statistics, ORF-length distribution, and lack of any periodicity are all consistent with random/non-coding DNA. If a feature was expected here, the data say this is almost certainly a featureless or randomly generated sequence — **nothing stands out.**
